paragraphs: We are transforming the way therapeutics and materials are discovered.

Our differentiated, physics-based computational platform enables discovery of high-quality, novel molecules for drug development and materials applications more rapidly and at a lower cost, compared to traditional methods. Our software platform is licensed by biopharmaceutical and industrial companies, academic institutions, and government laboratories around the world. We are applying our computational platform to advance a broad pipeline of drug discovery programs in collaboration with leading biopharmaceutical companies. In addition, we use our computational platform to discover novel molecules for our pipeline of proprietary drug discovery programs, which we are advancing through preclinical and clinical development.

Traditional drug discovery and development efforts are complex, lengthy and capital-intensive, and are prone to high failure rates. Traditional drug discovery relies upon many iterations of costly and time-consuming manual molecule design, chemical synthesis, and experimental testing. One of the primary reasons for long timelines, high costs, and high failure rates in drug discovery is that predicting properties of molecules in advance of chemical synthesis is extremely complex and not amenable to traditional approaches.

Over the past several decades and with the concerted efforts of our scientists and software engineers, we have developed a physics-based computational platform that is capable of predicting critical properties of molecules with a high degree of accuracy. This key capability enables drug discovery teams to design and selectively synthesize molecules with more optimal properties, reducing the average time and costs required to identify a development candidate and increasing the probability that a drug discovery program will enter clinical development. Furthermore, we believe that development candidates with more optimized property profiles will have a higher probability of success in clinical development. Additionally, since the physics underlying the properties of drug molecules and materials is the same, we have been able to extend our computational platform to materials science applications in fields such as aerospace, energy, semiconductors, electronic displays, and chemicals.

We offer our customers a variety of software solutions that accelerate all stages of molecule discovery, design, and optimization. In 2025, all of the top 20 pharmaceutical companies, measured by 2024 revenue, which we refer to as our top 20 pharma industry cohort, licensed our solutions, accounting for $73.7 million, or 37%, of our software revenue and $80.8 million, or 41%, of our annual contract value, or ACV, in 2025. The widespread adoption of our software, supported by our global team of sales, technical, and scientific personnel, has driven growth in our software business. Our ability to expand within our customer base is demonstrated by the increasing average ACV from our commercial customers with an ACV of over $1.0 million. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we had 27 commercial customers with an ACV of at least $1.0 million compared to 29 such customers for the year ended December 31, 2024. The average ACV per commercial customer with an ACV of over $1.0 million grew to $3.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $3.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. We believe the scaling up among the largest customers within our commercial customer cohort demonstrates that companies are increasingly recognizing the power and appreciating the scientific and financial benefits of using our platform at scale and the continued value of our platform. Our commercial customer cohort includes all of our customers purchasing our computational software solutions for commercial use, excluding government and academic institutions and customers from which we derive contribution revenue. See "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Key Factors Affecting Our Performance" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Change in Key Operating Metrics" for additional information regarding these operating metrics, including ACV and our industry and customer cohorts.

We also leverage our platform and capabilities across a portfolio of collaborative and proprietary drug discovery programs spanning a wide range of disease targets and indications. Our drug discovery group, which we refer to as the Schrödinger therapeutics group, is comprised of a multidisciplinary team of experts in protein science, biochemistry, biophysics, medicinal and computational chemistry, and discovery scientists with expertise in preclinical and early clinical development. We have entered into drug discovery collaborations with biopharmaceutical companies under which our collaborators are pursuing research in a number of therapeutic areas, including programs in oncology, antifungal diseases, fibrosis, inflammatory bowel disease, metabolic disease, autoimmune disease, immuno-oncology, cardiopulmonary disease, CNS diseases, and tuberculosis. When we engage in drug discovery with these collaborators, we typically provide

access to our platform and platform experts who assist the drug discovery collaborator in identifying molecules that have activity against one or more specified protein targets. Our collaboration agreements typically include upfront consideration, discovery, development, commercial and regulatory milestones, and royalties from future sales of commercialized products. We generate drug discovery revenue through the performance of specified research and development activities under our collaboration agreements and upon the achievement of discovery and development milestones, and we have the potential to generate drug discovery revenue from commercial and regulatory milestones, option fees, and royalties under our collaboration agreements. We also rely on collaborators for the development and potential commercialization of product candidates we discover internally when we believe it will help maximize clinical and commercial opportunities for the product candidate.

For example, in November 2024, we entered into a research collaboration and license agreement with Novartis Pharma AG, or Novartis, pursuant to which we and Novartis agreed to collaborate on the discovery, research and preclinical development of small molecule compounds for targets in certain specified therapeutic areas. The agreement is intended to advance multiple development candidates for development and commercialization by Novartis. We are eligible to receive up to $2.272 billion in total milestones across the initial programs, of which no milestone revenue has been recognized as revenue as of December 31, 2025, as well as a tiered percentage royalty on net sales of each product commercialized by Novartis ranging from mid-single-digits to low double-digits, subject to certain specified reductions. See "—Collaboration Agreement with Novartis Pharma AG" for additional information relating to this agreement. We also entered into a three-year software agreement with Novartis that substantially increased Novartis' access to our computational predictive modeling technology and enterprise informatics platform.

In 2018, we began to develop a pipeline of proprietary drug discovery programs with the goal of using our platform to produce a portfolio of novel, high value therapeutics. In June 2022, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or the FDA, cleared our first investigational new drug application, or IND, for our MALT1 inhibitor, which we refer to as SGR-1505. We have initiated dosing in a Phase 1 clinical trial of SGR-1505, which is designed as an open-label, multi-center dose escalation trial in patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. The trial is designed to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, maximum tolerated dose, maximum administered dose and/or recommended dose of SGR-1505. Backfill cohorts evaluate additional pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, preliminary anti-tumor activity and safety to support the recommended dose.

In March 2024, we also submitted an IND to the FDA for our novel Wee1/Myt1 inhibitor, which we refer to as SGR-3515, and the FDA cleared the IND in April 2024. We have initiated dosing in a Phase 1 clinical trial of SGR-3515 in patients with advanced solid tumors. The trial is a dose-escalation trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and recommended Phase 2 dose of SGR-3515. Secondary and exploratory objectives of the trial include evaluating the pharmacokinetics and preliminary anti-tumor activity of SGR-3515. We anticipate reporting initial data from the trial in the second quarter of 2026.
We plan to explore strategic partnerships for the SGR-1505 and SGR-3515 programs to advance the development of these programs beyond our ongoing Phase 1 clinical trials.

In August 2025, we announced the discontinuation of the clinical development program for SGR-2921, our CDC7 inhibitor, which was being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation clinical trial in patients with relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia, or AML, or high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes. Despite early evidence of monotherapy activity observed in the Phase 1 clinical trial, based on the profile observed prior to discontinuation, including two emergent events where SGR-2921 was considered to have contributed to two deaths in patients with AML, we determined the path to development as a combination therapy would be difficult to pursue.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated total revenue of $255.9 million and had a net loss of $103.3 million.

If our existing customers do not renew their licenses, do not buy additional solutions from us, or renew at lower prices, our business and operating results will suffer.
Our software sales cycle can vary and be long and unpredictable.
A significant portion of our revenues are generated by sales to life sciences industry customers, and factors that adversely affect this industry could adversely affect our software sales.
The markets in which we participate are highly competitive, and if we do not compete effectively, our business and operating results could be adversely affected.
If we are unable to collect receivables from our customers, our operating results may be adversely affected.
Defects or disruptions in our solutions could result in diminishing demand for our solutions, a reduction in our revenues, and subject us to substantial liability.
Any failure to offer high-quality technical support services could adversely affect our relationships with our customers and our operating results.

We may never realize a return on our investment of resources and cash in our drug discovery collaborations.

We have a history of significant operating losses. Our net losses for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 were $103.3 million and $187.1 million, respectively. Our net income for the year ended December 31, 2023 was $40.7 million. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $628.8 million. The net income we generated in the year ended December 31, 2023 was primarily due to the gain recorded on the $147.2 million cash distributions we received from Nimbus on account of our equity stake in Nimbus, following the acquisition by Takeda Pharmaceuticals Company, Limited, or Takeda, of Nimbus Lakshmi, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nimbus, and its TYK2 inhibitor NDI-034858 and the non-cash gain on our investment in Structure Therapeutics Inc., or Structure Therapeutics, which, following Structure Therapeutics' initial public offering in February 2023, we valued based on the closing price of its American Depositary Shares as of December 31, 2023. However, the potential for future distributions from, or gains in the fair value of, our equity stakes in our drug discovery collaborators are difficult to predict due to the inherent uncertainty of the events which may trigger such distributions or gains. We therefore expect that gain or loss on equity investments and fair value gains and losses will fluctuate significantly in future periods.

We anticipate that our operating expenses will increase in the foreseeable future as we continue to invest in our proprietary drug discovery programs, sales and marketing infrastructure, and our computational platform. We are still in the early stages of development of our own proprietary drug discovery programs. We have no drug products approved or licensed for commercial sale, and as such, have not generated any revenue from our own drug product sales to date. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and operating losses over the next several years. Our operating expenses and net income or loss may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year and you should not rely upon the results of any quarterly or annual periods as indications of future results. The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations covers fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 items and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. Discussions of fiscal 2023 items and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, that was filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025.

We are transforming the way therapeutics and materials are discovered. Our differentiated, physics-based computational platform enables discovery of high-quality, novel molecules for drug development and materials applications more rapidly and at a lower cost, compared to traditional methods. Our software platform is licensed by biopharmaceutical and industrial companies, academic institutions, and government laboratories around the world. We are applying our computational platform to advance a broad pipeline of drug discovery programs in collaboration with leading biopharmaceutical companies. In addition, we use our computational platform to discover novel molecules for our pipeline of proprietary drug discovery programs, which we are advancing through preclinical and clinical development.

Since our founding, we have been primarily focused on developing our computational platform, which is capable of predicting critical properties of molecules with a high degree of accuracy, as well as advancing drug discovery programs both with our collaborators and on our own. We have devoted substantially all of our resources to introducing new capabilities and refining our software, conducting research and development activities, recruiting skilled personnel, and providing general and administrative support for these operations.

Over the last decade, we have entered into a number of collaborations with leading biopharmaceutical companies that have provided us with significant revenue and have the potential to produce additional milestone payments, option fees, and future royalties. In 2018, we began to develop a pipeline of proprietary drug discovery programs with the goal of using our platform to produce a portfolio of novel, high value therapeutics.

In June 2022, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, cleared our first investigational new drug application, or IND, for our MALT1 inhibitor, which we refer to as SGR-1505. Our ongoing Phase 1 clinical trial of SGR-1505 is designed as an open-label, multi-center dose escalation trial in patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. The trial is designed to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, maximum tolerated dose, maximum administered dose and/or recommended dose of SGR-1505. Backfill cohorts evaluate additional pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, preliminary anti-tumor activity, and safety to support the recommended dose.

In April 2024, the FDA cleared the IND we submitted for our novel Wee1/Myt1 inhibitor, which we refer to as SGR-3515. In July 2024, we initiated dosing in a Phase 1 clinical trial of SGR-3515 in patients with advanced solid tumors. The trial is a dose-escalation trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability and recommended Phase 2 dose of SGR-3515. Secondary and exploratory objectives of the trial include evaluating the pharmacokinetics and preliminary anti-tumor activity of SGR-3515. We anticipate reporting initial data from the trial in the second quarter of 2026.

In August 2025, we announced the discontinuation of the clinical development program for SGR-2921, our CDC7 inhibitor, which was being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation clinical trial in patients with relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia, or AML, or high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes. Despite early evidence of monotherapy activity observed in the Phase 1 clinical trial, based on the profile observed prior to discontinuation, including two emergent events where SGR-2921 was considered to have contributed to two deaths in patients with AML, we determined the path to development as a combination therapy would be difficult to pursue.

Beyond our planned investments to complete our ongoing Phase 1 dose-escalation clinical trials of SGR-1505 and SGR-3515, we do not intend to initiate additional clinical trials or advance our other proprietary preclinical programs into clinical trials independently. We plan to explore strategic partnerships for the SGR-1505 and SGR-3515 programs to advance the development of these programs beyond our ongoing Phase 1 clinical trials. The phasing out of independent clinical development activities and associated cost reductions, together with the restructuring of our operations we announced in May 2025, which is further described below under "—Restructuring," are expected to result in total savings of approximately $70 million and further improve and enhance our operational efficiency.

In July 2024, we launched an initiative to expand our computational platform to predict toxicity associated with binding to off-target proteins. The goal of this initiative is to develop a computational solution designed to improve the properties of drug development candidates and reduce the risk of development failure associated with binding to off-target proteins, which can be associated with serious side effects. The project is being funded initially by $19.5 million in grants from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. We continue to advance our predictive toxicology initiative and have made the beta version available to customers, which encompasses approximately 50 representative kinases in addition to multiple key anti-targets. We expect to launch our predictive toxicology solution commercially and make it available more broadly to our customers during 2026.

We have funded our operations to date principally from the sale of our equity securities, including our initial public offering and our follow-on public offering, and to a lesser extent, from sales of our software solutions and from upfront payments, research funding and milestone payments from our drug discovery collaborations, and from distributions on account of, or proceeds from the sale of, our equity stakes in our collaborators. In 2023, on account of our equity stake in Nimbus Therapeutics, LLC, or Nimbus, we received an aggregate of $147.2 million in cash distributions from Nimbus in connection with Takeda's acquisition of Nimbus Lakshmi, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nimbus, and its TYK2 inhibitor NDI-034858.

On August 15, 2024, Morphic Holding, Inc., or Morphic, one of our drug discovery collaborators and co-founded companies, was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company, or Lilly, for $57.00 per share, or approximately $3.2 billion. In connection with the acquisition, we received $47.6 million for the 834,968 shares of Morphic we owned. We are also entitled to low single-digit royalties on our clinical development programs under our collaboration agreement with Morphic, including MORF-057.

paragraphs: 我們正在改變藥物及材料的發現方式。
我們的差異化、基於物理學的計算平台，使我們能更快速且以較低成本發現高品質、創新分子，用於藥物開發及材料應用，與傳統方法相比。我們的軟體平台已授權給全球的生物製藥與工業公司、學術機構及政府實驗室。我們正運用我們的計算平台，與領先的生物製藥公司合作，推進廣泛的藥物發現計畫。此外，我們也運用我們的計算平台，發現創新分子，用於我們的專屬藥物發現計畫，並透過臨牀前及臨牀開發階段進行推進。
傳統的藥物發現與開發過程複雜、耗時且資金密集，且失敗率高。傳統的藥物發現依賴許多次昂貴且耗時的手動分子設計、化學合成與實驗測試。導致藥物發現過程時間長、成本高、失敗率高的主要原因之一，是預測分子在化學合成前的特性極其複雜，且傳統方法難以應對。

在過去數十年，並透過我們科學家與軟體工程師的共同努力，我們已開發出一個基於物理學的計算平台，能以高度準確性預測分子的關鍵特性。此關鍵能力使藥物發現團隊能設計並選擇性合成具有更優化特性的分子，減少識別開發候選分子所需的平均時間與成本，並提高藥物發現計畫進入臨牀開發的機率。此外，我們認為具有更優化特性組合的開發候選分子，在臨牀開發中成功的機率更高。另外，由於藥物分子與材料的物理特性基礎相同，我們已能將我們的計算平台應用於材料科學領域，例如航空、能源、半導體、電子顯示及化學等領域。

我們為客戶提供多種軟體解決方案，加速分子發現、設計與優化的所有階段。2025年，根據2024年營業收入排名的前20大製藥公司，我們稱之為我們的前20大製藥產業羣組，皆已授權我們的解決方案，佔我們軟體營收的73.7 百萬美元，或37%，以及2025年年度合約價值（ACV）的80.8 百萬美元，或41%。我們軟體的廣泛採用，配合我們全球銷售、技術與科學團隊的支持，已推動我們軟體業務的成長。我們在客戶羣內擴張的能力，透過我們商業客戶的平均ACV增加可見一斑，這些客戶的ACV超過1.0 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們有27個商業客戶的ACV至少為1.0 百萬美元，與截至2024年12月31日的29個這樣的客戶相比。平均而言，ACV為1.0 百萬美元以上的商業客戶的ACV，截至2025年12月31日為3.9 百萬美元，與截至2024年12月31日的3.3 百萬美元相比。我們認為，在我們商業客戶羣組中最大的客戶規模擴張，顯示公司越來越認同我們平台的強大，並欣賞使用我們平台在規模上的科學與財務效益，以及我們平台的持續價值。我們的商業客戶羣組包括所有購買我們計算軟體解決方案用於商業用途的客戶，除外政府與學術機構及我們從中獲得貢獻收入的客戶。請參閱「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論—影響我們表現的關鍵因素」及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論—關鍵營運指標的變動」以取得關於這些營運指標的更多資訊，包括ACV及我們的產業與客戶羣組。

我們也運用我們的平台與能力，跨多個合作與專屬的藥物發現計畫，涵蓋廣泛的疾病目標與適應症。我們的藥物發現小組，我們稱之為Schrödinger藥物發現小組，由具備蛋白質科學、生物化學、生物物理學、藥物化學與計算化學以及具備臨牀前與早期臨牀開發經驗的發現科學家的跨領域專家組成。我們已與生物製藥公司簽訂藥物發現合作協議，這些合作夥伴正在進行多個治療領域的研究，包括癌症、抗真菌疾病、纖維化、炎症性腸道疾病、代謝疾病、自身免疫疾病、免疫腫瘤學、心肺疾病、神經系統疾病及結核病的計畫。當我們與這些合作夥伴進行藥物發現時，我們通常會提供

我們平台的存取及平台專家的協助，協助藥物發現合作夥伴識別對一個或多個指定蛋白質目標具有活性的分子。我們的合作協議通常包括前期報酬、發現、開發、商業與法規里程碑，以及未來商業化產品銷售的版稅。我們透過執行合作協議中指定的研究與開發活動，以及達成發現與開發里程碑，產生藥物發現收入，並有潛力透過商業與法規里程碑、選項費及版稅，在合作協議中產生藥物發現收入。我們也依賴合作夥伴進行我們內部發現的產品候選藥物的開發與潛在商業化，當我們認為這有助於最大化產品候選藥物的臨牀與商業機會時。

例如，在2024年11月，我們與Novartis Pharma AG（Novartis）簽訂了一項研究合作與授權協議，根據協議，我們與Novartis同意合作進行特定治療領域中小型分子化合物的發現、研究與臨牀前開發。此協議旨在推動多個開發候選藥物的開發與商業化。我們有資格獲得總計達22.72 億美元的里程碑報酬，截至2025年12月31日，尚未有里程碑報酬被認列為收入，以及Novartis商業化每項產品的淨銷售額的階梯式百分比版稅，範圍從中單位數到低雙位數，視特定條件而有所減少。請參閱「—與Novartis Pharma AG的合作協議」以取得關於此協議的更多資訊。我們也與Novartis簽訂了一項三年期的軟體協議，大幅增加了Novartis對我們計算預測模型技術與企業資訊科技平台的存取權。

2018 年，我們開始發展一項專屬的藥物發現計畫，目標是利用我們的平台來產生一組具創新性且高價值的治療藥物。2022 年 6 月，美國食品藥物管理局，或稱為 FDA，核准我們第一項新藥申請，或稱為 IND，針對我們的 MALT1 抑制劑，我們稱為 SGR-1505。我們已啟動 SGR-1505 的第一期臨牀試驗，試驗設計為開放標籤、多中心的劑量遞增試驗，針對患有復發或難治性 B 細胞惡性腫瘤的病患。試驗設計用以評估 SGR-1505 的安全性、藥動學、藥效學、最大耐受劑量、最大給藥劑量及/或建議劑量。補充族羣則評估額外的藥動學、藥效學、初步抗腫瘤活性及安全性，以支持建議劑量。

2024 年 3 月，我們也向 FDA 提交了我們新型 Wee1/Myt1 抑制劑 SGR-3515 的 IND，FDA 於 2024 年 4 月核准了該 IND。我們已啟動 SGR-3515 的第一期臨牀試驗，針對患有晚期實體腫瘤的病患。試驗為劑量遞增試驗，設計用以評估 SGR-3515 的安全性、耐受性及建議的第二期試驗劑量。試驗的次要及探索性目標包括評估 SGR-3515 的藥動學及初步抗腫瘤活性。我們預期在 2026 年第二季報告該試驗的初步數據。
我們計畫探討 SGR-1505 和 SGR-3515 計畫的戰略合作夥伴，以推動這些計畫超越我們目前進行的第一期臨牀試驗。

2025 年 8 月，我們宣佈終止 SGR-2921 的臨牀發展計畫，SGR-2921 是我們的 CDC7 抑制劑，正在進行一項針對患有復發/難治性急性髓細胞白血病，或稱為 AML，或高風險骨髓增生異常綜合症的病患的第一期劑量遞增臨牀試驗。儘管在第一期臨牀試驗中觀察到單一療法的活性，但根據終止前觀察到的資料，包括兩起事件中 SGR-2921 被認為可能導致 AML 病患死亡，我們認為發展為組合療法的路徑將非常困難。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們產生總營業收入 255.9 百萬美元，並產生淨虧損 103.3 百萬美元。

paragraphs: 你應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與本年度財務報表及相關附註一同參考。部分資訊包含於本討論與分析或本年度報告其他處，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略之資訊，均為涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。
下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析涵蓋財務年度2025與財務年度2024之項目，以及財務年度2025與財務年度2024之年對年比較。財務年度2023之項目與財務年度2024與財務年度2023之年對年比較，未包含於本Form 10-K之內容，可於我們財務年度終結於2024年12月31日之年度報告Form 10-K，於第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」中找到。
因許多因素，包括於第一部分，第1A項「風險因素」中所列示之因素，我們實際結果可能與下列討論與分析中所描述或暗示之展望性陳述結果有重大差異。有關我們展望性陳述之進一步資訊，請參閱本年度報告中「展望性陳述與產業資料之警示說明」。

我們正在改變藥物與材料之發現方式。我們獨特的、基於物理學之計算平台，使我們能更快、以更低的成本發現高品質、創新之分子，用於藥物開發與材料應用，與傳統方法相比。我們之軟體平台被全球之生物科技藥品與工業公司、學術機構與政府實驗室所授權。我們正運用我們之計算平台，與領先之生物科技藥品公司合作，推進廣泛之藥物發現計畫。此外，我們亦運用我們之計算平台，發現創新分子，用於我們之專屬藥物發現計畫，並透過臨牀前與臨牀開發階段進行推進。
自我們成立以來，我們主要專注於發展我們之計算平台，該平台能以高準確度預測分子之關鍵特性，以及與合作夥伴與自行推進藥物發現計畫。我們已投入幾乎所有資源於引入新功能與改善軟體、進行研究與開發活動、招募專業人才，並提供一般及行政支援以執行這些業務。
在過去十年中，我們已與多家領先之生物科技藥品公司建立合作關係，這些合作關係為我們帶來顯著收入，並有潛力產生額外之里程碑付款、選項費與未來版稅。2018年，我們開始發展專屬之藥物發現計畫，目標為運用我們之平台產生一組創新、高價值之治療藥物。

2022年6月，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准我們首個新藥研發申請（IND），即我們所稱之SGR-1505 MALT1抑制劑。我們持續進行SGR-1505之第一期臨牀試驗，設計為開放標籤、多中心劑量遞增試驗，用於治療復發或難治性B細胞惡性腫瘤患者。該試驗設計用以評估SGR-1505之安全性、藥動學、藥效學、最大耐受劑量、最大給藥劑量及/或建議劑量。補充羣組評估額外之藥動學、藥效學、初步抗腫瘤活性及安全性，以支持建議劑量。
2024年4月，FDA核准我們提交之新型Wee1/Myt1抑制劑IND申請，我們所稱之SGR-3515。2024年7月，我們在患有晚期實體腫瘤之患者中開始進行SGR-3515之第一期臨牀試驗劑量遞增試驗。該試驗設計用以評估SGR-3515之安全性與耐受性及建議之第二期試驗劑量。試驗之次要與探索性目標包括評估SGR-3515之藥動學與初步抗腫瘤活性。我們預期於2026年第二季報告該試驗之初步資料。

2025年8月，我們宣佈終止SGR-2921的臨牀開發計畫，SGR-2921為本公司開發的CDC7抑制劑，當時正在進行一項針對復發/難治性急性骨髓性白血病，或AML，或高風險骨髓增生異常綜合症患者的第1期劑量遞增臨牀試驗。儘管在第1期臨牀試驗中觀察到單獨使用時的活性，但根據終止前觀察到的資料，包括兩起事件中SGR-2921被認為與AML患者兩例死亡有關，我們認為以組合療法方式進行開發的路徑將難以持續進行。

除我們預計用於完成我們持續進行的 Phase 1 劑量遞增臨牀試驗的 SGR-1505 和 SGR-3515 之外，我們不打算啟動其他臨牀試驗或獨立推動我們其他專利前期臨牀計畫進入臨牀試驗。我們計畫探討策略性合作夥伴關係，以推動 SGR-1505 和 SGR-3515 計畫的發展，超越我們持續進行的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗。獨立臨牀發展活動的逐漸減少及相關成本降低，加上我們於 2025 年 5 月宣佈的營運重整，進一步說明如下 "—重整," 預期將導致總共節省約 70 百萬美元，並進一步提升和增強我們的營運效率。

2024年7月，我們啟動了一項計畫，以擴展我們的計算平台，用以預測與非目標蛋白結合相關的毒性。此計畫的目標是開發一個計算解決方案，用以改善藥物開發候選物的特性，並降低與非目標蛋白結合相關的開發失敗風險，這可能與嚴重的副作用有關。此專案最初由比爾及梅琳達·蓋茨基金會提供的19.5 百萬美元補助金資助。我們持續推進預測毒理學計畫，並已將Beta版本提供給客戶，該版本涵蓋約50個代表性激酶以及多個關鍵抗目標。我們預期於2026年推出預測毒理學解決方案，並更廣泛地提供給客戶。

截至目前為止，我們的運作資金主要來自我們的股票發行，包括我們的首次公開發行及後續公開發行，以及較少程度來自我們軟體解決方案的銷售，以及來自我們藥物發現合作夥伴的前期付款、研究資金及里程碑付款，以及來自我們合作夥伴的股票權益分紅或出售所得。2023年，因我們在Nimbus Therapeutics, LLC，或Nimbus的股票權益，我們從Nimbus收到總計147.2 百萬美元的現金分紅，與Takeda收購Nimbus Lakshmi, Inc.，為Nimbus的全資子公司，及其TYK2抑制劑NDI-034858有關。

2024年8月15日，Morphic Holding, Inc.，或Morphic，為我們的藥物發現合作夥伴及共同創辦公司之一，被Eli Lilly and Company，或Lilly，以每股57.00美元，或約3.2 十億美元收購。與此收購相關，我們因擁有Morphic的834,968股股票而收到47.6 百萬美元。我們也根據與Morphic的合作協議，對我們的臨牀開發計畫，包括MORF-057，有低個位數的版稅權利。
目前，我們透過兩個應報告分部進行運作：軟體及藥物發現。軟體分部專注於銷售我們的軟體，用以轉變生命科學產業的藥物發現，以及

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求
本公司有持續產生重大營運虧損的歷史，且預期在未來數年內仍將產生虧損。
本公司每季及每年的營運結果可能出現顯著波動，這可能會對本公司普通股的價值產生不利影響。
籌措額外資金可能會導致股東權益稀釋、限制本公司營運，或要求本公司放棄對智慧財產權或藥物開發計畫的所有權。
與本公司軟體相關的風險
若現有客戶未續約許可證、未購買額外解決方案，或以較低價格續約，將會對本公司營運及營運結果造成負面影響。
本公司軟體銷售週期可能變化且長且難以預測。
本公司收入的相當大一部分來自生命科學產業客戶的銷售，而影響此產業的不利因素可能會對本公司軟體銷售產生不利影響。
我們參與的市場競爭激烈，若我們無法有效競爭，將可能對本公司業務及營運結果產生不利影響。
若我們無法從客戶收取應收帳款，將可能對本公司營運結果產生不利影響。
我們解決方案中若有瑕疵或中斷，將可能導致對我們解決方案的需求減少，營業收入下降，並使本公司面臨重大賠償責任。
若無法提供高品質的技術支援服務，將可能對本公司與客戶的關係及營運結果產生不利影響。
與藥物發現相關的風險
我們可能永遠無法實現對資源及現金投資於藥物發現合作計畫的回報。
我們可能無法實現對本公司在藥物發現合作夥伴中之股權投資的回報。
我們可能無法成功進行識別、發現或開發產品候選藥物，並可能無法把握具更大商業機會的計畫、合作或產品候選藥物。
paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並與本年度年報及其他所有資訊一併考量，同時也應參考我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的其他公開申報文件。下列所描述的風險並非本公司唯一面臨的風險。上述任何風險，或尚未為我們所知或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，若發生，可能會導致本公司業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況遭受重大影響。

我們預期在可預見的未來，本公司營運費用將持續增加，因我們持續投資於專屬藥物發現計畫、銷售與市場推廣基礎設施，以及我們的計算平台。我們目前仍處於開發自有專屬藥物發現計畫的初期階段。我們目前尚未有核准或取得許可可供商業銷售的藥物產品，因此截至目前為止，尚未從自有藥物產品銷售中產生任何收入。我們預期在接下來的幾年內，仍將持續產生重大費用與營運虧損。本公司營運費用以及淨收入或虧損，可能在每個季度與年度之間有顯著波動，您不應依賴任何季度或年度的結果作為未來結果的指標。我們預期，若我們：
•持續投資並發展我們的計算平台與軟體解決方案；
•持續進行自有專屬藥物發現計畫之研究與開發工作；
•進行任何產品候選藥物之預臨牀研究與臨牀試驗；
